metadata.headline: ‘Play Dirty’ Review: A Halfhearted Heist Movie
metadata.speaker: am

sentences.sentence: The blunt comedy “Play Dirty,” Shane Black’s adaptation of Donald E.
Westlake’s Parker crime novels, is a faint shadow of the director’s best work.

It stars Mark Wahlberg as Parker, the taciturn thief whose team is eradicated by a fellow robber named Zen (Rosa Salazar), following a caper whose careening car chase into a horse track gives a taste of the film’s hollow spectacle.

When a vengeful Parker tracks down Zen, he learns she’s planning to steal a billion dollars' worth of artifacts and jewels from a recently rediscovered 15th-century ship to feed those starving in an unnamed Latin American country.

Putting aside their animosity, Parker and Zen assemble a gang in New York that includes a theatrical Grofield (LaKeith Stanfield) to devise a plan that, on top of the heist, will avoid the wrath of The Outfit, a crime syndicate led by Lozini (Tony Shalhoub), that is illegally selling the artifacts on behalf of the crooked president (Alejandro Edda).
